newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia stocks end 1.5 pct up in broad rebound.
newsitem.headline: Australia stocks end 1.5 pct up in broad rebound.

text.p: *Stocks broadly up in quiet trade in rebound from recent losses. Bonds, results fuel gains. Volume 315.64 million, A$651.08 million value, 1,073 stocks traded, 287 steady, 511 up, 275 down.

The Australian share market ended on a firm node on Friday as stocks rebounded from losses earlier in the week, supported by a stronger bond market, postive earnings reports and some talk about another official rate cut.

The All Ordinaries index rose 38.8 points to 2,666.2, but still 1.7 percent down on the week. September share price index futures climbed 44 points to 2,662, a 4.2 point discount to the underlying index. Turnover was a modest A$651 million.
"The market had taken quite a beating this week, and people were generally calling it up today. Every sector rose quite solidly," one senior institutional dealer in Sydney said.
Brambles rose 90 cents to A$27.70 and helped the tranport sector index rise 2.6 percent.

Another winner was Mayne Nickless, up 22 cents to A$8.26 on increasing hopes of a quick sale of its 25 percent stake in Optus Communications after a government decision to ease foreign shareholder restrictions in Optus.
News Corp climbed sevem cents to A$5.95 ahead of its results on Wednesday, while Fairfax rose three to A$3.19 pending the earnings report on Tuesday.
Great Central Mines rose five cents to A$2.57 after dismissing rumours of a takeover bid from Barrick Gold.
